original_question: On which chromosome is the gene whose mutations cause retinoschisis located?

final_qi.question: On which chromosome is the gene whose mutations cause retinoschisis located?
final_qi.long_answer: X-linked juvenile retinoschisis is caused by mutations in the RS1 (retinoschisin) gene, which is mapped to the short arm of the X chromosome at Xp22.2. Therefore, the gene responsible for retinoschisis resides on the X chromosome.

final_answer.long_answer: X-linked juvenile retinoschisis is caused by mutations in the RS1 (retinoschisin) gene, which is situated on the short arm of the X chromosome (Xp22.1). Because the gene is X-linked, affected males display the retinal splitting characteristic of the disease, while carrier females are typically asymptomatic.
